title: "What does the reconstructed airframe actually look like?"
---

{{< include _model.qmd >}}

```{python}
ENTRY_CEILING = 120.0   # s for this render, granted by the user
SOLVE_BUDGET = 15.0     # s for any one solve
PROBE_POOL = 200.0        # s granted for the probe
PROBE_SPENT = 4.1      # s the probe actually used

import aerosandbox.tools.pretty_plots as p

# Geometric properties of the reconstructed airframe
b_w = wing.span()
S_w = wing.area()
c_mac = wing.mean_aerodynamic_chord()
taper_w = c_tip_wing / c_root_wing
l_fuse = fuse.length()
S_wet_fuse = fuse.area_wetted()
n_fuse_xsecs = len(fuse.xsecs)
b_h = htail.span()
S_h = htail.area()
b_v = vtail.span()
S_v = vtail.area()
```

**Answer.** The reconstructed airframe reproduces the semi-scale layout of a P-51 Mustang with a low-wing tractor configuration (@fig-reconstructed-three-view). The tapered wing spans [`{python} f"{b_w*1e3:.0f} mm"`]{.key} with [`{python} f"{S_w*1e2:.2f} dm²"`]{.key} planform area, a taper ratio of [`{python} f"{taper_w:.2f}"`]{.key}, and [`{python} f"{dihedral_deg:.1f}°"`]{.key} dihedral. The [`{python} f"{l_fuse*1e3:.0f} mm"`]{.key} fuselage features [`{python} f"{n_fuse_xsecs}"`]{.key} cross-section stations capturing the radiator belly scoop and canopy deck, totaling [`{python} f"{S_wet_fuse*1e2:.2f} dm²"`]{.key} wetted area. The conventional empennage mounts a [`{python} f"{b_h*1e3:.0f} mm"`]{.key} horizontal stabilizer and an [`{python} f"{b_v*1e3:.0f} mm"`]{.key} vertical fin.

```{python}
#| label: fig-reconstructed-three-view
#| fig-cap: "Orthographic three-view and isometric projection of the reconstructed airframe."
fig, axs = p.figure3d(nrows=2, ncols=2, figsize=(7.5, 7.5), computed_zorder=False)
_ = airplane.draw_three_view(axs=axs, show=False)
```
